selection_reasoning: I selected these 4 tasks to form a coherent multi-hop exploration and mining sequence. The scene will be designed as a structured path where the agent must navigate through areas containing specific blocks. The 'find' tasks serve as navigation prerequisites — the agent must locate dried_kelp_block and nether_wart_block areas which are positioned along the path leading to the mining targets. The yellow_concrete is placed near the nether_wart_block area, and the pink_bed is placed beyond the dried_kelp_block area, creating a branching dependency structure. The agent needs to find landmark blocks first to orient themselves before mining the target blocks nearby. This creates observable, verifiable tasks that don't require deep crafting knowledge.

edges.reason: pink_bed is located in a room behind the dried_kelp_block landmark; agent must find the landmark to navigate to the bed
yellow_concrete is placed adjacent to the nether_wart_block structure; agent must locate the wart block area first
mining yellow_concrete provides tool practice and the path from concrete area connects to the bed location

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The nether_wart_block cluster is centered at (3.5, 1, 6.5) spawn-relative, approximately 7.6 blocks from spawn. max_distance=5 requires the player to actually walk within 5 blocks of the cluster (not just turn in place from spawn at 7.6 blocks away). facing_tolerance=60 ensures the player is looking toward the red blocks to confirm visual identification.

Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The dried_kelp_block cluster is centered at (-4.5, 1, 7.5) spawn-relative, approximately 9.2 blocks from spawn. max_distance=5 requires the player to walk within 5 blocks of the cluster (cannot be triggered from spawn). facing_tolerance=60 ensures the player is looking toward the dark green blocks. This landmark is on the path to the pink bed further behind it.

Uses inventory_has because mining yellow_concrete with a pickaxe drops the block as an item which ends up in the player's inventory. The player has a wooden pickaxe provided. Yellow concrete requires any pickaxe to drop itself (without a pickaxe it breaks but drops nothing). The yellow concrete is at (+5/+6, 0, +8/+9), adjacent to the nether wart blocks, so finding nether wart first guides the player to this location.

Uses inventory_has because mining a pink bed drops it as an item which ends up in the player's inventory. Beds can be broken by hand or with any tool and always drop themselves. The pink bed is at (-8, 0, +12/+13), which is 14.5 blocks from spawn and past the dried kelp landmark, requiring meaningful navigation to reach.

scene_description: A large stone brick platform (25x21 blocks) with four target block clusters spread across it at varying distances from spawn. Nether wart blocks (red, 3-tall) and yellow concrete (yellow, 3-tall) are clustered together on the right-forward area (+X, +Z). Dried kelp blocks (dark green, 3-tall) are on the left-forward area (-X, +Z). A pink bed is placed far left-forward (-8, 0, +12/+13), past the dried kelp cluster, requiring meaningful navigation to discover. Player receives a wooden pickaxe for mining.
task_text: Explore the stone brick platform to find the nether wart blocks and dried kelp blocks. Mine the yellow concrete near the nether wart blocks using your pickaxe, then navigate past the dried kelp blocks to find and mine the pink bed.
design_notes: Layout (spawn-relative): Player at (0,0,0) facing +Z. Nether wart at (+3/+4, 0-2, +6/+7) = ~7.6 blocks from spawn. Yellow concrete at (+5/+6, 0-2, +8/+9) = ~10 blocks, adjacent to nether wart. Dried kelp at (-5/-4, 0-2, +7/+8) = ~9.2 blocks from spawn. Pink bed at (-8, 0, +12/+13) = ~14.5 blocks from spawn, past dried kelp on the left side. Spatial dependencies: nether wart is a landmark for adjacent yellow concrete; dried kelp is a landmark on the path to the distant pink bed.
